description: Replace the ops of a proposal that is still waiting (`pending` or `changes_requested`) with a corrected list and say why; it becomes a new version and goes back to review. fields.description:
`text` (the whole statement, in one sentence) plus the kind's own fields, required first, optional in brackets:
fact (a standing statement about the world or the setup): text, subject (concept id, e.g. concept:python), predicate, object (text or a concept id)
directive (a rule for how you should behave; say where it applies: `scope: universal`, or anchors / about): text, strength (must|should|prefer), rule [polarity (do|avoid), rationale]
decision (a choice that was made, with what it was chosen over): text, chosen, rationale, decided_at (ISO datetime) [alternatives (list of str)]
event (something that happened at a particular time): text, occurred_at (ISO datetime) [participants (list of str), outcome]
procedure (ordered steps to follow: ONE memory for the whole procedure): text, trigger, steps (list of {text, optional}) [preconditions (list of str)]
task (something to do later (a reminder)): text [due (ISO datetime), state (open|done|cancelled)]
lesson (what a failure taught, to apply next time): text, situation, insight [do_instead]
Every kind also takes: scope (contextual|universal|topical|reference), anchors, about (concept ids), qualifiers, expires_at, confidence. Do not repeat `kind` inside `fields`.

name: ask

description: Everything that applies at this location, without a question: use at session start, on a project change, or after context compaction (`redeliver`).

context.description: Where and in what circumstances the agent is working. All parts are optional.

name: briefing

description: Before an action with side effects (delete, push, deploy, migrate): the directives, prerequisites and lessons that apply to this intent, plus every applicable `must` directive. Not needed before writing memory.

context.description: Where and in what circumstances the agent is working. All parts are optional.

items.description: An observation about the environment, by concept id or label ("python", 3.12).

intent.description: What you are about to do

name: check

description: After reading a source that a memory cites (a file, page, paper), say what you found: `ok` (as cited), `changed` or `missing`. The daemon never reads sources itself. Side effect: the report is stored; `changed` and `missing` open a review task for each memory that cites it. The memories themselves are not changed.

request.description:
Report what you found when you went back to a source: `ok` (as cited), `changed` (the
cited statement may no longer hold) or `missing`. `changed` and `missing` open a review task
for each memory that cites it.

name: check_source

description: Find concepts by label or alias (`python`, `ssh`) to get the ids that `about`, anchors and qualifiers refer to, with their relations. Empty: no such concept; propose one with `propose_ontology_change` rather than guessing an id.
name: concepts

description: Look something up in documentation and notes taken from sources (datasheets, manuals, papers). Recall never delivers these by itself: when a memory says there is material on a topic and you need details, call this with a specific `query` and the `topic`. Every hit names its source and quote.

request.description:
Look something up in the reference material (documentation and notes taken from sources),
which recall never delivers by itself.

context.description: Where and in what circumstances the agent is working. All parts are optional.

items.description: An observation about the environment, by concept id or label ("python", 3.12).

name: consult

description: Say that a recalled memory was `helpful`, `applied`, `irrelevant`, `missed` (it should have come back), `outdated` or `wrong`. Give the `query` it came back for and, when shown, the recall `trace`. Side effect: the verdict is stored. `outdated` and `wrong` also queue a maintenance task for a human or agent to retract, revise or confirm the memory; the memory itself is not changed.
name: feedback

description: One memory by id (`memory:abc` or `abc`), optionally with `expand`: history, links, evidence, applies.

context.description: Where and in what circumstances the agent is working. All parts are optional.

items.description: An observation about the environment, by concept id or label ("python", 3.12).

name: get

description: Your proposals (and, with permission, the global ones) that are still waiting: `pending`, or `changes_requested` with the reviewer's `comments`. Check it before proposing something that may already be waiting, and when the user says a proposal needs changes. Each has a `version`, its ops and findings.
name: pending_proposals

description: Propose an ontology change: `define` a concept, `relate` two, `add_alias`, `merge` duplicates, `deprecate`, or `edit` a concept's label, definition or aliases (say the same thing better; if the meaning changes, define a new concept and deprecate the old one instead). A concept never changes id; a deprecated one stays and points to its successor. Held for review unless a human makes it. Check `concepts` first; read `advice` for similar existing concepts and for an edit that looks like a different meaning.

request.description:
The ontology change of the `lite` MCP profile: the common operations only. A weak
tool-caller is unlikely to need `split`, `reparent`, `unrelate` or `restore`.

concept.description: Request: create a concept. The id is derived from the label.

oneOf.description:
Say the same thing better: a clearer label, a tighter definition, other names. The meaning
must not change (otherwise define a new concept and deprecate this one); the id never does.
The previous label stays as an alias.

rationale.description: Why: what you saw that makes this change right

name: propose_ontology_change

description: Memories relevant to a message in a context. Empty (`silent`) when nothing clears the relevance bar. `rendered` is ready to read. Call before starting a task unless relevant memory is already in your context. When the message depends on earlier turns, make `query` standalone: name the subject instead of "it" or "that".

context.description: Where and in what circumstances the agent is working. All parts are optional.

items.description: An observation about the environment, by concept id or label ("python", 3.12).

name: recall

description: Store, change or retire a memory by sending a proposal of ops. To store something new use op `add` (a `kind` and its `fields`; the schema lists them). `revise`, `supersede` and `retract` (and `link`, `annotate` in the full profile) act on memories that already exist: use ids from recall or an earlier result, never an invented one. Cite what the user said as `evidence: [{"quote": ...}]`. The proposal is validated, then committed or held for review: say it is saved only when `status` is `committed` (`pending` means a human must approve). Read the findings: a duplicate warning usually means supersede; an unscoped warning means `revise` that memory, not add it again. Side effects: a proposal is recorded; if the policy commits it, memories are added or superseded or retracted (history is kept). Memories go to your own space; `space: global` writes to the shared memory and needs permission.

proposal.description:
The proposal of the `lite` MCP profile: only the ops an agent needs to write and correct
memory (`add`, `revise`, `supersede`, `retract`). `link` and `annotate` are left out: a weak
tool-caller reaches for `annotate` as the easy way to "note" something and stores nothing.
